title: GANTZ:G
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A high school class dies when their bus plunges off a bridge and wakes in a room with a black sphere that sends them, armed and suited, to fight grotesque aliens for points that can buy back a life. Lead Kei Kurona fights to earn enough to revive the boy she likes, while classmates face bullying, a stalker and an abusive parent. A three-volume spin-off of Hiroya Oku's Gantz, drawn by Keita Iizuka; published by Dark Horse.
life_message: Survival tests who people really are, and courage and loyalty under pressure can let them grow past cruelty and fear.

content.note: ANN reviewers call it graphic, 'ridiculously gory ultraviolence' with cruel deaths; AniList Gore, MU Blood and Gore.
Play-or-die alien hunts and sudden deaths of classmates (AniList Survival; MU Kill or Be Killed; ANN).
ANN reviewers flag 'blatant sexualization of the young female cast'; MU Nudity, Attempted Rape; MangaDex rates it erotica.
Gantz sphere taunts and berates players (ANN); profanity level not reported (to verify).
Bullying, stalking and an abusive father among classmates' backstories (ANN).

dominant: Death-game survival; cruelty of power; courage under pressure

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Personal combat decides worth; the sphere scores and berates players (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Players are bound by the sphere's rules and missions.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to classmates and one beloved boy rather than family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Points ranking and an all-powerful sphere.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Kill-or-be-killed survival is the whole frame (MU).

folkways.japan: Uses familiar Japanese school-class dynamics, including peer rumor and exclusion, inside a seinen death-game format.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers find the treatment of bullying and abuse surface-level; neither calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Themes are carried by action and backstory rather than argument.

winners_losers: Survivors who fight hardest win points and second chances; bullies and bystanders tend to lose; sympathy goes to Kei and the bullied girls.
